what_happened: After the 4.6 s handoff on a multi-lane highway with no conflict ahead (the lead car was 20+ m away and pulling away), the ego braked hard (17 to 8 m/s) and veered left out of its lane, away from the recorded path. Its front-left corner hit actor 1, which was travelling in the adjacent left lane. The hard, unnecessary braking probably also explains the rear contact flagged for this run.

On an open highway after handoff, the policy braked hard for no clear reason (29 → 13 m/s), which got it rear-ended. It then steered left across the left edge line onto the shoulder and median, while the recorded path and the RIGHT command led the other way. By 7.7 s it was off the road, about 4.9 m from the recording, with the trailing car 40 overlapping it.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s, the ego braked hard for no clear reason, slowing from about 16 to 8 m/s while the car ahead (actor 18) was pulling away. At the same time it drifted left off its route into the left lane, and its front hit actor 1, which was beside it and slightly ahead in that lane.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s on a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (16.6 to 9.0 m/s with the lead 20+ m away and pulling ahead), and its planned path swung left. Actor 1 in the left lane drew level, and the ego's front-left corner drove into it. The recorded human path, and the RIGHT command at the end, went straight or to the right. The ego was also hit from behind, probably as a result of its own sudden braking.

On a straight multi-lane highway after handoff, the policy braked hard for no clear reason (28 to 13 m/s with the lead 30–46 m ahead) and steered left, away from the recorded path, which kept to the right. The route command switched to RIGHT, but the ego kept drifting left until it went off the left edge of the road at 7.9 s, clipping actor 40 as it did (front-contact flag set in the same frame). The ego was also rear-ended at some point, probably a result of the sudden braking, but the failure counted here is leaving the road.

On a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, the ego slowed from 6.8 to 4.4 m/s and drifted left, away from the recorded path (green ego box left of the grey ghost). Car 41 was passing in the lane to its left, and the ego's front corner hit it at 7.1 s.

On a multi-lane highway, the policy's plan drifted left toward the adjacent left lane while the recorded path went straight. It slowed from 6.8 to 4.1 m/s as it moved over, and its front hit pickup 41, which was passing on the left (the ego ended about 1.3 m left of the recorded path).

On a multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path bent left while it slowed from about 6.8 to 4.5 m/s, and the ego drifted toward the lane on its left. Its front then struck the pickup (actor 41) driving alongside in that lane. The recorded human path stayed in the original lane, and the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, so nothing called for a move to the left.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard from 29 to 13 m/s and, instead of keeping right as the recorded route did (the command turned to RIGHT), steered left across the lanes. By 7.8 s it had reached the left edge near the median barrier, where it went off-road and clipped a vehicle (id 10) in front of it, about 5 m from the recorded path; something had also hit the ego's rear earlier in the run.

After handoff the policy braked hard on the highway (28 → 13 m/s) and was rear-ended, and its planned path kept drifting left even though the route went straight and then RIGHT. By 7.9s the ego had crossed the left lane edge onto the median shoulder, about 5 m off the recorded path, and was flagged offroad.

The command was RIGHT, but after handoff the policy steered left, away from the recorded path, and merged into the lane to its left. Actor 28 was driving alongside in that lane, and the ego's front hit it at 8.4 s at about 6.7 m/s.

In slow, queued city traffic, the ego drifted about 2.8 m right of the recorded path so it straddled the lane line, and it kept creeping forward (0.8 m/s down to 0.3 m/s) instead of stopping. Its front clipped the rear corner of stopped car 24, which was ahead and slightly to its left.

On a highway with a RIGHT command, the policy braked hard (from 26.5 to 12.9 m/s) and steered left, away from the recorded path on the right. It drifted onto the left edge line and shoulder and went offroad at 8.1 s, about 5 m from the recorded path. A car hit the ego's rear at some point; the rear-collision flag was already set by 6.1 s, and the hard braking at highway speed may have caused it. The rear hit did not push the ego off the road.

After handoff the ego braked hard (29→13 m/s) with no close lead and got rear-ended, which was not its own fault. It then drifted left across the leftmost lane line onto the shoulder/median even though the route said RIGHT and its planned path went right, and it went offroad at 7.7s, where actor 40 also overlapped it.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted left off its planned path (5 m off the recorded trajectory) and into the adjacent left lane while slowing from about 10 to 6 m/s. Its front struck vehicle 28, which was travelling in that lane just ahead and to its left.

Going straight in slow, queued traffic, the ego slowed from 1.8 to 0.1 m/s but never came to a full stop. It kept creeping toward the stopped car ahead (actor 24), as the gap shrinking from 6.4 m to 4.6 m shows, until its front touched that car at 10.1 s.

The ego was in a slow queue going STRAIGHT and kept creeping toward stopped car 24 ahead in its lane, slowing from 1.8 to 0.1 m/s while the gap shrank from 6.4 to 4.6 m. It never fully stopped and made low-speed front contact with car 24's rear, about 2.9 m off the recorded human path. The right side of the camera view was smeared, but the lead car was clearly visible.

In slow, queued traffic, the ego rolled forward behind stopped car 24 in its lane and drifted about 2.9 m right of the recorded path. It slowed from 2 m/s but did not stop short, and at 9.8 s its front bumper touched 24's rear at a crawl (0.1 m/s).

After handoff, on a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left instead of following the recorded path toward the right lanes, ending about 5 m off the human trajectory. While slowing from about 10 to 6.5 m/s, it moved into the adjacent left lane, and its front hit vehicle 28 in that lane, which had come alongside from behind-left.

The command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted left of the recorded path, about 5 m off it by the failure, and ended up straddling the lane line on its left while slowing from 9 to 7 m/s. Vehicle 28 was passing on the left in that lane, came alongside and then ahead, and at 8.4 s the ego's front hit it.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted left out of its lane on the multi-lane freeway, about 5 m from the recorded path. Vehicle 28 was coming up and passing on the left, and the ego's front hit it as the ego moved into its lane at about 6.4 m/s. A rear contact on the ego was also recorded, but the front collision came first and was caused by the ego's lane change.

On the highway with a RIGHT command, the ego slowed behind car 36 and then steered left across the lane line, away from the recorded path. It ran its front into car 28, which was travelling in the lane to the left right beside it.
